title: AIPAC-Linked Super PACs, Pro-Israel Donors Flood Primary to Succeed Angie Craig With More Than $3 Million
author: Julian Andreone
content:
[![](https://substackcdn.com/image/fetch/$s_!zwYD!,w_1456,c_limit,f_auto,q_auto:good,fl_progressive:steep/https%3A%2F%2Fsubstack-

Rep. Kaela Berg, Sen. Matt Klein, and Matt Little on the stage during a
Congressional Candidate Forum at Minnesota Farmfest in Morgan, Minn., on
Tuesday, August 4, 2026. Photo by Carlos Gonzalez/The Minnesota Star Tribune
via Getty Images.

Four super PACs with ties to AIPAC and Democratic Majority for Israel have
surged into a Minnesota House race in the final months of the campaign, hoping
to fend off the latest progressive insurgent.

In the three-way race, one candidate, Matt Klein, is unapologetically
supportive of Israel, while two others, Matt Little and Kaela Berg, have been
critics to varying degrees. Little, however, has the support of the group A
New Policy, which was founded to support pro-Palestinian candidates and lobby
Congress against Israeli interests. Another PAC, called American Priorities,
which was organized to be a counterweight to AIPAC, [has jumped into the
race](https://x.com/RobletoFire/status/2085449864696000662) to support Little
with a spend of some $60,000.

314 Action, a super PAC ostensibly organized to support scientists and medical
professionals, [this week reported spending nearly $2.5
million](https://docquery.fec.gov/cgi-bin/forms/C00633248/2004730/se)
supporting Klein, a staggering amount in a previously sleepy race, given that
the PAC has raised just $15 million for the full cycle. (A spokesperson for
314 insists none of the funds have come from AIPAC or its allied
organizations.)

In a strategy that has been deployed in other races, the pro-Israel money is
boosting Klein, the pro-Israel candidate, while other PACs with ties to AIPAC
are boosting the alternative progressive candidate who is trailing in the
polls.

The race was reshaped on May 9, when Little won the endorsement of the
Minnesota Democratic Farmers and Labor Party. Little released an internal
survey conducted between May 18 and 20, which found him well ahead, taking 41%
of the vote, with Berg and Klein far behind in a statistical tie for second,
with Berg at 13% and Klein at 11%. A little more than a week later, Klein
fielded his own poll, which found Little at 26%, only 7 points over Klein's
19%. Berg was in third with 16%. The largest group of the 403 likely voters
surveyed in the poll, 39%, said they "don't know" who they'd vote for. While
Klein's internal poll demonstrates that Little was firmly the frontrunner in
the race two months before election day, it was conducted before the surge in
outside spending began.

The congressional seat is being vacated by Democrat Angie Craig, who is
running for Senate. The primary is on Tuesday.

Given the numbers, the path to victory for Klein was clear: He needed Little
to be brought down by boosting Berg--splitting the vote between the two
progressives--and needed big money to get himself past both of them.

On May 1, [AIPAC's super PAC had transferred
](https://www.fec.gov/data/receipts/?data_type=processed&committee_id=C00863472&contributor_name=C00799031)$350,000
to EDW Action Fund, followed by $100,000 on May 10 and another $400,000 on May
20. EDW did not respond to requests for clarification on why the money was
moved and where it was ultimately spent.

EDW Action [spent](https://www.fec.gov/data/independent-
expenditures/?data_type=efiling&committee_id=C00685297&committee_id=C00949248&candidate_search=berg&is_notice=true&most_recent=true)
roughly $395,000 supporting Berg between June 26 and August 3. Of the $395,000
burned, $99,999 came directly from EDW and $295,000 came from its sister
organization called Pro-Choice Majority Action, a hybrid PAC recently formed
on May 1 as a legal affiliate of EDW Action. EDW [transferred $626,000 and
$100,000](https://docquery.fec.gov/cgi-bin/fecimg/?202606209870850976) to Pro-
Choice Majority Action on May 21 and May 22 respectively, on the two days
after receiving the final batch of AIPAC's $850,000 dump, and sent another
$150,000 a week later on May 29, helping to enable Pro-Choice Majority's
ensuing spending.

Moving money between multiple PACs before spending it doesn't necessarily make
it much harder to trace, but it does make it more confusing for voters and
local reporters covering the race. AIPAC, for its part, [accuses
reporters](https://x.com/AIPAC/status/2060751056385053084?s=20) of
antisemitism for following AIPAC money through the FEC files toward its final
destination. Candidates like Little risk being called conspiracy theorists
when they point to the clear source of the money. Indeed, after Drop Site
reached out to Berg's campaign for comment, Berg [posted a video on
X](https://x.com/kaelaberg/status/2085158543125106723) accusing Little of
lying about her and insisting that she doesn't take AIPAC money: "I never
have, and I never will."

It is true she has not taken AIPAC money directly, but on May 13, four days
after Little won the DFL endorsement, DMFI transferred
[$500,000](https://www.fec.gov/data/disbursements/?data_type=processed&committee_id=C00710848&recipient_name=C00473918&two_year_transaction_period=2026&min_date=01%2F01%2F2025&max_date=12%2F31%2F2026)
to Women Vote, the independent expenditure arm of EMILY's List, a pro-choice
PAC. Then, less than a month later, Women Vote [spent $584,448 in independent
expenditures](https://www.fec.gov/data/independent-
expenditures/?data_type=processed&most_recent=true&q_spender=C00473918&is_notice=true&candidate_id=H6MN02271&candidate_id=H6MN02230&candidate_id=H6MN02248)
supporting Berg.

"Women Vote works with a variety of partners to elect Democratic pro-choice
women and build winning coalitions," a source familiar with Women Vote's
spending told Drop Site. "The donation referenced was for a program in a
different race and has nothing to do with Kaela Berg or this race."

Sara Nelson, head of the Association of Flight Attendants-CWA, AFL-CIO, told
Drop Site that unions raised outside support for Berg, also drawing from gun
safety, pro-democracy, and pro-choice donors, using Women Vote as the vehicle.
A coalition including EDW, Women Vote, and labor unions announced $500,000 in
spending for Berg on May 20.

Little told Drop Site that if Berg believes Israeli is committing a genocide
in Gaza, she should reject funding from organizations like Women Vote and EDW
Action, who take money from AIPAC and DMFI, even if those groups say that
particular money was not used in her particular race. "Let's say all of that
is opaque…and we can't really tie that to Berg," he said. "We have called on
Representative Berg to say to her PACs publicly, stop taking AIPAC money. I
don't want you to take AIPAC money and if you continue to take AIPAC money, I
am going to reject your endorsement and give the money back."

Though the Women Vote source did not disclose the recipient of the $500,000,
Women Vote did spend a total of $653,885 supporting Shannon Bird, a [DMFI-
endorsee](https://demmajorityforisrael.org/dmfi-focusing-ire-on-anti-israel-
democrats-running-in-swing-districts/), in her unsuccessful bid to become the
Democratic nominee in Colorado's 8th congressional district. Despite securing
DMFI's endorsement, Bird, who ultimately lost to Manny Rutinel, [does not list
the PACs support on her website](https://shannonbird.com/endorsements/).

Nevertheless, the total dollars spent on Berg's behalf by PACs that have been
used as pro-Israel passthroughs at some point, including Women Vote, amounts
to $979,448 since June 11. Now, the fact that PACs linked to AIPAC are
spending to boost Berg doesn't mean Berg herself is aware of the links, and
doesn't mean pro-Israel donors affirmatively want Berg to win. DMFI, when
reached for comment, rejected any involvement with Women Vote's support for
Berg's campaign.

"DMFI PAC endorsed Matt Klein in this race. Kaela Berg's views are equally as
anti-Israel as Matt Little's," a DMFI spokesperson told Drop Site.

A Berg spokesperson rejected any relation between these groups' spending in
the race and the pro-Israel lobby's donations to the spenders.

"Matt Little agrees with Kaela on Israel and AIPAC, that's why AIPAC is
funneling millions in dark money into this race at the 11th hour to support
Matt Klein," the spokesperson told Drop Site. "As the only woman running for
Congress, Kaela is proud to have the support of the same organizations that
have supported Peggy Flanagan and every woman in the MN Congressional
Delegation. The truth is, Benjamin Netanyahu continues to be a danger to the
world and if she's elected to Congress, Kaela will do everything in her power
to stop the genocide and Netanyahu's government."

Berg has earned support from three state senators, 28 of her colleagues in the
Minnesota House of Representatives, and national progressive organizations
like Our Revolution and End Citizens United. She's supported by many unions,
too: the Association of Flight Attendants, Communications Workers of America,
the Association of Professional Flight Attendants, the Carpenters Union, UNITE
HERE, United Auto Workers, the Air Line Pilots Association, the International
Association of Sheet Metal, Air, Rail, and Transportation Workers, the
Amalgamated Transit Union, local members of the International Brotherhood of
Teamsters, United Steelworkers, and the International Union of Painters and
Allied Trades. She has also received some support from D.C., racking up
endorsements from Rep. Chris Deluzio, who [many speculate is eyeing a primary
challenge](https://www.post-gazette.com/news/politics-state/2026/08/07/john-
fetterman-primary/stories/202608060054) to Sen. John Fetterman (D-Penn.) in
2028, and Rep. Val Hoyle (D-Ore.).

Aside from securing the coveted Minnesota DFL endorsement, Little has also
picked up backing from the state's Attorney General Keith Ellison, and key
figures within the existing progressive infrastructure in Congress. Rep. Greg
Casar, chair of the Congressional Progressive Caucus, Rep. Pramila Jayapal,
former CPC chair, and Rep. Maxwell Frost, one of CPC's vice chairs, have all
publicly supported his candidacy.

The CPC's PAC is also supporting Little.

Klein, for his part, has also seen a flood of supportive outside spending. 314
Action Fund is a super PAC which backs candidates who are involved in science
or medicine, but has [sometimes acted in the past
](https://theintercept.com/2024/05/04/aipac-congress-the-squad/)as an AIPAC
passthrough. FEC records show that the super PAC
[spent](https://www.fec.gov/data/independent-
expenditures/?data_type=processed&most_recent=true&q_spender=C00633248&is_notice=true&candidate_id=H6MN02248&candidate_id=H6MN02230)
$1,261,341 in independent expenditures backing Klein in four installments
between July 20 and July 30. On August 5, 314 Action dropped another $1.2
million into the race.

The state senator has also received an additional $138,440 from 57 individual
donors who have also given to AIPAC, UDP, or DMFI. All of the individual
donations were [given on the same
day](https://www.fec.gov/data/receipts/?data_type=processed&committee_id=C00904292&contributor_name=Gadi+Maier&contributor_name=James+Sprayregen&contributor_name=aaron+goldman&contributor_name=adam+reich&contributor_name=alan+shamah&contributor_name=ira+riklis&contributor_name=jody+forchheimer&contributor_name=larry+kugler&contributor_name=lawrence+greenberg&contributor_name=nathan+lindenbaum&two_year_transaction_period=2026&min_date=06%2F28%2F2026&max_date=06%2F28%2F2026),
June 28, many divided in various increments amounting to the maximum $3,500
individual contribution each.

Among those individuals is James Sprayregen, who sits on the National Board of
AIPAC and serves on the Board of Governors for the American Jewish Committee.
Sprayregen contributed $129,500 to the pro-Israel groups and to Klein in three
separate same-day installments amounting to $3,499.99, one cent below the
legal maximum, possibly to avoid being classified as a max-out donor.

Also listed among the individual donors pooled by AIPAC on Klein's behalf are
Jody Forchheimer, who gave $283,456 to pro-Israel PACs and $3,500 to Klein,
and Gadi Maier, who gave $135,000 to pro-Israel PACs and $3,500 to Klein.
Forchheimer is a Senior Legal Fellow at the Louis D. Brandeis Center, a pro-
Israel legal organization fighting antisemitism cases, and publicly discussed
her role in pro-Israel advocacy at the AIPAC policy conference in 2019. Maier
is an Israeli-American tech entrepreneur who is founder and CEO of ID
Handshake, the first and a current board member at Forter, a fraud prevention
platform, and formerly served as CEO of both FraudSciences and FreeMonee.

When asked about 314 Action Fund backing Klein's campaign and an inquiry about
the aforementioned prominent pro-Israel donors, the campaign manager provided
a statement in response to the latter.

"Our campaign is powered by thousands of supporters from every background and
every faith--because that's who we are, and that's who I've spent my career
serving," Klein told Drop Site. "As a doctor, I've cared for Jewish families,
Muslim families, Christian families, and families of no faith at all, and I've
never once asked who they were before helping them. This campaign is no
different. I'm proud of the support we've received from neighbors, community
leaders, and working families of all denominations."

Addressing the first question, the spokesperson added, "You should talk with
314 about their funding. I have copied Eden from their team on this email."

The move was eyebrow-raising, as campaigns and independent expenditure groups
are not allowed to coordinate campaign activity. Though it is not considered
best practice for campaigns and independent expenditure arms to communicate at
all, it is legal to discuss some information as long as it doesn't amount to
coordination.

314 Action also received a $2.5 million donation from pro-Israel billionaire
Michael Bloomberg on May 4, just months before its spending blitz in
Minnesota. Whether Bloomberg's money is earmarked to the Klein race is
unclear; it would be odd if so, as Berg is endorsed by the organization
Everytown for Gun Safety, which Bloomberg founded and primarily finances. That
would mean Bloomberg was spending against himself in the same race.

Joshua Morrow, 314 Action Fund's president, said in a statement that the group
is not funneling pro-Israel PAC money into the race. "As we have said multiple
times, 314 Action Fund has not taken money from AIPAC or its affiliated
entities this cycle and we won't," Morrow said. "We have spent over $14.5
million supporting STEM candidates in 2026 and not a cent has come from AIPAC,
UDP, DMFI or affiliated entities. Similarly, our investments in Dr. Matt Klein
are not from AIPAC or affiliated entities, and any suggestion otherwise is
false, sensationalized and reported without sources."

Still, Klein refuses to recognize the genocide in Gaza, instead broadly
calling for a two-state solution. Berg and Little, backed by David Hogg's
Leaders We Deserve, on the other hand, have publicly called it one. Little
differentiates himself from Berg, however, in supporting a suspension on any
further U.S. military aid to Israel, while the latter has [advocated for
conditioning it](https://kaelaforcongress.com/issues/#elementor-toc__heading-
anchor-5). In a video posted Wednesday, she calls for an end "to all weapons
sales to Israel," going further than she had previously.

Klein has racked up endorsements from 19 colleagues in the Minnesota state
senate, but has not received any explicit endorsements from Washington. The
two-term state senator has also faced some scandal in the race, having placed
a $50 wager on Kalshi, a prediction market service, betting that he'd win the
MN-02 primary, which ultimately led to an April 2026 fine and five-year ban
from the platform. Klein introduced an ultimately unsuccessful bill in the
state legislature in 2024 that would have weakened regulations on sports
gambling, a highly profitable path for companies like Kalshi.

_**Update, Saturday, August 8:** This story was updated to reflect additional
context around the spending provided by AFA President Sara Nelson._
